topic_and_scope: A focused appraisal of brain glycogen metabolism, its astrocyte-dominant storage, lactate shuttle to neurons, and implications for synaptic plasticity, sleep, injury responses, and neurological diseases, with an emphasis on therapeutic avenues and measurement challenges.
main_themes: Cellular and network physiology of brain glycogen metabolism and astrocyte–neuron metabolic coupling
Role of glycogen dynamics in memory, synaptic plasticity, sleep regulation, and responses to metabolic stress
Therapeutic strategies and diagnostic challenges targeting glycogen metabolism in neurological disorders
main_findings: Brain glycogen, predominantly stored in astrocytes, supports rapid energy supply to neurons via glycogenolysis and astrocyte-to-neuron lactate shuttling, with regional heterogeneity and relevance to memory, sleep, and stress responses.

Alterations in brain glycogen metabolism are associated with epilepsy, neurodegenerative diseases (AD, PD, ALS), and congenital disorders (Lafora disease); while mechanistic links are established, precise in vivo quantification and cell-type–specific roles remain incompletely defined.

key_gaps.description: In vivo quantification of brain glycogen remains technically challenging, with limited spatial resolution and sensitivity across regions and cell types.
Mechanistic understanding of cell-type–specific glycogen dynamics (astrocytes vs neurons) and the lactate shuttle under various disease conditions is incomplete, hindering targeted therapies.

future_directions.title: Develop advanced in vivo imaging and metabolomics to quantify brain glycogen at cellular resolution
future_directions.rationale: Current in vivo methods struggle with sensitivity and spatial precision. A concerted effort should combine multimodal imaging (enhanced MRS, PET tracers), novel glycogen-specific probes, and longitudinal metabolomics to map regional glycogen distribution and dynamic changes during sleep, hypoglycemia, and disease. Validation should occur across animal models and human subjects to enable reliable cross-species comparisons and enable monitoring of therapeutic interventions.

future_directions.title: Dissect astrocyte-specific glycogen metabolism and lactate shuttle in epilepsy models
future_directions.rationale: Epilepsy is linked to altered glycogen dynamics and astrocyte-to-neuron lactate supply. Utilize astrocyte-specific glycogen synthase knockouts or chemogenetic control of astrocytic glycolysis to assess seizure frequency, neuronal excitability, and cognitive outcomes. Combine with ketogenic diet and pharmacologic modulators to determine whether boosting astrocytic glycogen output or lactate delivery attenuates seizures.

future_directions.title: Elucidate glycogen-derived lactate signaling pathways in memory consolidation
future_directions.rationale: Glycogen-derived lactate supports LTP and hippocampal memory. Identify whether lactate acts through receptor-mediated mechanisms or intracellular signaling (e.g., CREB, MAPK) and determine region-specific effects. Experimental approaches should include manipulating lactate production/uptake during learning tasks and profiling downstream signaling and synaptic protein phosphorylation.

future_directions.title: Characterize sleep–glycogen dynamics across aging and neurodegenerative risk
future_directions.rationale: Glycogen metabolism fluctuates with sleep and modulates memory processes; longitudinal studies should correlate region-specific glycogen changes with sleep stages and cognitive trajectories in aging and disease models. Interventions targeting sleep quality or glycogen cycling could be evaluated for their capacity to preserve memory and reduce cognitive decline.

future_directions.title: Develop brain-penetrant modulators of glycogen synthase and glycogen phosphorylase
future_directions.rationale: Therapeutic potential exists for enzyme-level modulation but faces safety and specificity concerns. Create selective, brain-penetrant compounds that selectively modulate glycogen synthase or phosphorylase, evaluate efficacy in epilepsy and neurodegenerative disease models, and conduct comprehensive safety and off-target assessments, including metabolic consequences on glial and neuronal circuits.

future_directions.title: Explore glial-targeted gene therapies to restore glycogen metabolism
future_directions.rationale: Gene therapy offers a route to correct glycogen storage and mobilization deficits in astrocytes. Develop glial-specific vectors (e.g., AAV with GFAP/ALDH1L1 promoters) to overexpress or normalize glycogen synthase activity, assess energy metabolism, neuroinflammation, and cognitive outcomes in relevant disease models, and monitor long-term safety.

future_directions.title: Investigate gut microbiota modulation as a lever to brain glycogen metabolism
future_directions.rationale: Microbiota-derived metabolites, especially SCFAs, may regulate glial metabolism and glycogen dynamics. Systematically evaluate probiotic/prebiotic regimens and fecal microbiota transplantation in models of epilepsy and neurodegeneration, measuring effects on glycogen availability, lactate signaling, neuroinflammation, and behavioral outcomes; aim to identify personalized microbiome-based strategies.

future_directions.title: Target congenital glycogen storage disorders with integrated metabolic therapies
future_directions.rationale: Lafora disease and Pompe-related CNS involvement illustrate profound glycogen dysregulation. Pursue disease-modifying approaches combining gene editing or gene therapy with enzymatic or dietary strategies, and optimize enzyme replacement therapy for CNS delivery where feasible. Preclinical evaluation should focus on neuronal/glial energy balance, autophagy, and neuroprotection, with progression toward early-phase clinical trials.
